speaker: Patient
text: 57-year-old male. The patient reports a large wound on his right lower leg that has been present for 6 months. He mentions that his legs have been chronically swollen for over 10 years and that his mother and brother had similar leg problems. He had a documented deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the affected leg 5 years ago but has no other significant past medical history.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The history of chronic swelling for 10 years, a prior DVT, and a family history of similar issues strongly suggests venous insufficiency. Given the wound is present for 6 months, I need to confirm its location and characteristics: is it located near the medial malleolus, and does it show signs of surrounding hemosiderin staining or hyperpigmentation?

REQUEST IMAGES: Right lower leg wound close-up.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Large wound on the right lower leg. I also have Chronic leg swelling, Family history of similar leg problems.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your history of chronic swelling, prior DVT, and family history, this picture strongly suggests a venous stasis ulcer due to chronic venous insufficiency. To confirm the diagnosis and assess the extent of the venous disease, I need to see the current image of the wound and order imaging.

REQUEST IMAGES: Right lower leg wound close-up.
REQUEST TEST: Venous Duplex Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: IMAGES: Right lower leg wound close-up shows a large ulcer on the right lower leg with surrounding skin discoloration and evidence of chronic changes. TEST: Venous Duplex Ultrasound (Doppler Ultrasound Lower Limb): Evidence of venous reflux and obstruction in superficial and deep venous systems of the right leg.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The ultrasound confirms significant venous reflux and obstruction, and the wound description shows chronic skin changes consistent with venous stasis. Based on the history of DVT, chronic edema, and the imaging findings showing venous insufficiency, I am ready to finalize the diagnosis.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Venous Insufficiency with Venous Stasis Ulcer.
